a: The most successful pirate in history is widely considered to be Henry Every, also known as 'Long Ben' or 'Captain Bridgeman,' who operated in the late 17th century. Every's most famous exploit was the capture of the Ganj-i-Sawai, a massive Mughal Empire treasure ship carrying gold, silver, and precious stones worth an estimated £600,000 — an amount so enormous that it caused an economic crisis in the Mughal Empire and prompted the English government to offer a massive reward for his capture. Every's success was remarkable not just for the scale of his loot but for his ability to evade capture for years despite being the most wanted man in the English-speaking world. He assembled a diverse crew of over 400 men from multiple nations and sailed across the Indian Ocean, striking at the wealthiest targets of the Mughal and Ottoman empires. After his final major raid in 1696, Every disappeared with his crew and treasure, and his fate remains a mystery — some believe he returned to England and lived in luxury under an assumed name, while others think he was killed in a Native American raid. Other highly successful pirates include Bartholomew Roberts, who captured over 470 ships during his three-year career, and Edward Teach, better known as Blackbeard, who terrorized the Caribbean and American colonies. However, Henry Every stands out for the sheer scale of his single heist, his ability to operate across multiple oceans, and his successful evasion of the most powerful naval forces of his time. His legend has endured for over three centuries, inspiring books, films, and countless stories of buried treasure.
